clue.text: Motor finally parked and up for nap, perhaps

parts.note: a motor is everyday British slang for a car

indicators.note: finally points at the closing letter of the word parked

parts.note: only its final letter is used
to be up for something is to be game for it

explanation.surface: Someone parks the car at last and is ready for a little sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: Nap looks like a snooze, but it is also the name of a trick-taking card game (Napoleon).
explanation.definitionFit: Nap is one example of a game played with cards, so the definition is by example, flagged by perhaps.

clue.text: Bosses as a group provide staff, mature chaps, over time

indicators.note: in a down clue the chaps sit over, that is above, the time abbreviation

parts.note: to man something is to supply it with workers
to age is to mature
men are chaps

explanation.surface: A description of the senior team staffing up with older men over a period.
explanation.definitionFit: The collective body of people running an organisation is its management, its executives taken together.

clue.text: Force into service a refined chap, one who'll manage the limelight

parts.note: to press someone is to conscript them, as the old press gangs did
taken as written
a gent is a gentleman

explanation.surface: A well-bred man is conscripted to handle someone's publicity.
explanation.definitionFit: A publicist arranges newspaper and broadcast coverage, steering how much spotlight a client receives.

clue.text: Without opening pick up win

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, which is taken away

parts.note: to pick up a skill is to learn it

explanation.surface: Someone tries to pick up a win without an opening.
explanation.walkthrough: GAIN also fits the crossers and means win, but its parse needs AGAIN for pick up, which does not hold; this key corrects it.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn is to obtain something through effort, as a reward or salary, so it matches win.

clue.text: Post first of messages with trouble

indicators.note: first of takes just the leading letter of messages

parts.note: only its first letter, M, is used
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Someone has difficulty with the first of their messages in the post.
explanation.definitionFit: Post and mail are the British and American names for the same letter-delivery service.

clue.text: Fix a place for squaddie to scoff

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the room where soldiers eat; a squaddie is a British private soldier and to scoff is to eat greedily

explanation.surface: Instructions to set up a spot where a soldier can eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A plight or jam is a mess, and the military dining hall is also called the mess.

clue.text: Several pickpockets

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an old word for various or several
second meaning: a diver is old slang for a pickpocket, who dives into pockets

explanation.walkthrough: The archaic adjective (as in 'divers places') and underworld slang for a thief are the two senses; it is not the swimmers.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers as an adjective means sundry or a number of, and as a noun it was thieves' cant for pickpockets.

clue.text: Zanzibari's first article found in bustling Arab market

indicators.note: found in says the following pieces sit inside the rearranged word
bustling suggests busy motion, so the letters of Arab are stirred up

parts.note: its letters are rearranged

indicators.note: first takes only the leading letter of Zanzibari's

parts.note: only its first letter is used
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A Zanzibar native's first purchase is spotted in a busy Arab souk.
explanation.definitionFit: A bazaar is an oriental marketplace of stalls, especially in the Middle East.

clue.text: Theoretical scholar

definitions.meaning: first meaning: of no practical relevance
second meaning: a university teacher or researcher

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it suggests a theorist; the two words are separate senses of one word, adjective and noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for something abstract and moot and a noun for a university lecturer.

clue.text: Current and mostly insensitive plan

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word is kept, its last letter dropped

parts.note: deaf can mean unmoved, as in deaf to pleas

explanation.surface: A scheme that is topical yet largely unfeeling.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea can be a scheme or intention, as in 'the idea is to leave early'.

clue.text: Aviators, say, crooned in front of girls

indicators.note: the singing word comes before the girls word in the answer

parts.note: crooned means sang softly
lasses are girls, chiefly in Scotland and northern England

explanation.surface: Pilots serenading some young women.
explanation.walkthrough: Aviators look like pilots; here they are the classic teardrop-shaped shades.
explanation.definitionFit: Aviators are a style of tinted eyewear, so they are one example of shades worn against the glare.

clue.text: Package of British booze

parts.note: ale is beer, a kind of booze

explanation.surface: A consignment of British drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A bale is a large bound bundle of goods such as hay or cotton.

clue.text: She serves on board and has stories which stagger

indicators.note: words that stagger reel about, so the letters of the phrase are jumbled

parts.note: its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cabin crew member with tales so striking they astonish.
explanation.walkthrough: Stagger seems to mean amaze, but here it is the letters that reel.
explanation.definitionFit: A stewardess on an aircraft serves passengers their food and drink during the flight.

clue.text: Galloped round here?

parts.note: rode on horseback at speed
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A question about the arena where riders charged about.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the place: cowboys gallop round the ring at such a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo is a cowboy contest of riding and roping, staged in an arena where horses gallop.

clue.text: What's said to unblock old writer's consistent energy first

indicators.note: first puts the energy letter ahead of the word for consistent

parts.note: a pen is a writer, so the possessive gives pen's
unchanging, the same throughout

explanation.surface: Advice on unblocking an elderly author's steady flow of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: The magic words from Ali Baba open the robbers' cave, so they are what's said to unblock.
explanation.definitionFit: The password in the Arabian Nights tale opens a sealed cave, so it is a phrase uttered to remove a barrier.

clue.text: Time nears to turn round cheat's copy

indicators.note: round says the reworked letters go around the cheat word
to turn means the letters of nears are turned about into a new order

parts.note: its letters are rearranged
a crib is a cheat sheet, and to crib is to cheat

explanation.surface: Time is running out for a cheat to make a copy.
explanation.definitionFit: To transcribe is to write out a copy of a text or recording, so it means reproduce.

clue.text: Widely circulated image is narcissist's preoccupation?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a picture or joke shared virally online
second meaning, cryptic: a self-obsessed person's constant thought, the first-person pronoun said twice

explanation.surface: A viral picture said to be the self-absorbed person's obsession.
explanation.walkthrough: Split in two, the answer is the pronoun a narcissist repeats endlessly about themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A meme is a picture or joke that spreads virally from user to user online.

clue.text: Brave Republican cancelled supply

indicators.note: something cancelled is struck out, so the Republican letter is removed

parts.note: to brave a storm is to endure it

explanation.surface: A courageous Republican calls off a delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: Brave looks like an adjective describing the Republican, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To endue is to provide or furnish someone with a quality, as in endued with talent.

clue.text: What's offered before deal is reflected in sweet nature

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the other way round, so the letters are read backwards
in says the letters are found inside the words sweet nature

parts.note: the letters sit across the two words

explanation.surface: Something offered before a deal mirrors a pleasant temperament.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker each player puts a stake into the pot before the cards are dealt.

clue.text: Altering broken instrument

indicators.note: the word is broken up and its letters rebuilt

parts.note: its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Changing an instrument that is damaged.
explanation.definitionFit: The triangle is a percussion instrument, a bent steel bar struck with a beater.

clue.text: I tout sci-fi being otherwise imaginary

indicators.note: otherwise means arranged differently, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fan promoting science fiction admits it is made up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fictitious is invented and not real, like the worlds of a novel.

clue.text: Animate popular quote

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in crowd
to cite is to quote

explanation.surface: Bring to life a well-liked quotation.
explanation.definitionFit: To incite is to stir up or rouse people, so it matches animate as a verb.

clue.text: Son to anoint ground

parts.note: to anoint is to smear with oil

explanation.surface: A boy is told to anoint the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Soil is the earth that plants grow in, the ground underfoot.

clue.text: Put a lid on what soldiers dip into? Savoury snacks

parts.note: to scotch a rumour is to stamp it out
soldiers here are British fingers of toast, dipped into soft-boiled eggs

explanation.surface: Suppressing what troops plunge into, plus some savoury bites.
explanation.walkthrough: Soldiers are strips of toast dipped into a boiled egg's yolk, not troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scotch egg is a hard-boiled egg wrapped in sausage meat and breadcrumbs, a popular British picnic food.

clue.text: This could be sweet but not small?

definitions.text: This could be sweet but not small?

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters may form something else once rearranged
but not tells us to take away the small abbreviation

parts.note: its remaining letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A riddle about something that might be cute without being tiny.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a twisted form of sweet itself, and means sickly sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee describes something excessively cute or quaint, a cloying kind of prettiness.

clue.text: Luvvies being phoney after top part's dropped

indicators.note: in a down answer the top letter drops to the foot of the word

parts.note: a sham is something fake

explanation.surface: Theatrical types who turn out fake once their head is gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Luvvies is British slang for gushing theatre people; ham actors overplay their parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Hams are actors who overact, and luvvies are affected thespians, so both name showy performers.

clue.text: Talk big about this dress

indicators.note: about here means turned about, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to brag is to boast

explanation.surface: Someone boasts about an outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is clothing of a distinctive kind, so it means attire.

clue.text: Female with this class would be up-front

indicators.note: the answer is what remains of the word once the female letter is added to it
would be links the answer plus the letter to the longer word

parts.note: frank means candid and open

explanation.surface: A woman of this social standing would speak openly.
explanation.walkthrough: Add the female abbreviation to the answer and it becomes a word for candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank is a grade or social standing, so it means class.

clue.text: Bold headline is right to go into chef's aid?

indicators.note: to go into says the right letter is placed inside the kitchen word

parts.note: a steamer is a pan used to steam food

explanation.surface: A question about whether a big headline should fit into kitchen kit.
explanation.walkthrough: In newspapers a streamer is a headline running across the whole page.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspapers call a large headline spanning the full page width a streamer or banner.

clue.text: Toy for tot's instant temper

parts.note: mo is short for moment
bile is bad temper, from the old humour

explanation.surface: A child's plaything triggers an instant tantrum.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobile is a hanging ornament of dangling shapes that turns above a baby's cot.
